title: Minimum Time to Visit All Houses
summary: Given two arrays forward and backward of size n, and an array queries, you must determine the minimum time to visit each house in the specified order.
statement: Given two arrays forward and backward of size n, and an array queries, you must determine the minimum time to visit each house in the specified order. Houses are arranged in a circle with connections defined by forward and backward arrays. For each query, calculate the total time to visit all houses, starting from house 0, moving at one meter per second, and considering the circular arrangement of the houses.
constraints: forward and backward describe directed clockwise and counterclockwise edge costs on a circle of up to 100,000 houses.
Start at house zero and visit query houses in order; every consecutive query target differs.
Return the minimum total travel time, choosing either direction independently for each leg.
hints: Between two houses on a directed circle, every simple route is either entirely clockwise or entirely counterclockwise.
Prefix-sum the two directional edge arrays and compute both wrap-aware arc costs for each requested leg.
Starting at zero, add min(clockwise(source,target), counterclockwise(source,target)) and advance source to target.
Positive edge costs make extra cycles useless, so one of the two simple directional arcs is always an optimal leg.
editorial: Positive edge costs make extra cycles useless, so one of the two simple directional arcs is always an optimal leg.

tests.explanation: The cheapest legs cost one, four, three, and four seconds, totaling twelve.
Walking one forward edge for every leg completes the tour in four seconds.
